Here’s a minimal pattern that works well for React/SPA pages and also fixes the “only top-level tag returned” issue: ```python import asyncio from crawl4ai import AsyncWebCrawler, CrawlerRunConfig, BrowserConfig from crawl4ai.async_configs import CacheMode async def main(): run_config = CrawlerRunConfig( # Make sure JS-heavy content has time to render wait_for_images=True, # also ensures images are fully loaded on most sites scan_full_page=True, # scrolls the page to trigger lazy-loaded content scroll_delay=0.5, # wait between scrolls so React/JS can render cache_mode=CacheMode.BYPASS, verbose=True, ) async with AsyncWebCrawler(config=BrowserConfig(headless=True)) as crawler: result = await crawler.arun("https://your-react-site.com", config=run_config) if result.success: # Full rendered HTML print(result.html[:2000]) # inspect first couple kb else: print("Error:", result.error_message) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ``` Relevant pieces from the docs: - `wait_for_images=True` makes the crawler “wait until images are fully loaded” before finalizing HTML, which implicitly gives JS/React more time to render.
